messages.content: Is there support for Special Learning Needs?

Yes, PolyU and the EEE department are committed to inclusivity. Academic Advisors are trained to identify students with special learning needs early on and make necessary referrals to university support services. We want to ensure every student has the environment they need to succeed.
I want to do research on cars. Who should I talk to?

You should look for **Prof. K.T. Chau** or **Prof. C.C. Chan**. They lead our **Research Centre for Electric Vehicles**. They are working on everything from in-wheel motors to wireless charging. If you are passionate about automotive engineering, there is no better place in Hong Kong to be.
如果我想创业，学系有支持吗？
有的。我们新成立了 **EEE 创新与工程中心 (Hub)**，专门支持学生的早期创业想法。我们可以提供导师指导，甚至帮你连接‘理大创客基金 (PolyU InnoHub)’。我们希望培养的不只是工程师，更是未来的企业家。
What is the 'Industrial Centre' I keep hearing about?

The Industrial Centre (IC) is one of PolyU's best facilities! It's a massive workshop where you actually get your hands dirty building things. You'll go there to learn practical skills like soldering, PCB fabrication, 3D printing, laser cutting, and even handling heavy machinery. It's quite different from just sitting in lectures—you're actually making stuff. Students love it because you come out feeling confident with real tools, not just theory. Fair warning though: IC sessions can be long and tiring, especially when you're debugging a circuit that won't work!
What programming languages will I need to learn?

You'll mainly use **Python** and **C/C++** - Python for data analysis and AI projects, C/C++ for embedded systems and hardware control. We also touch on MATLAB for signal processing. Don't worry if you're new to programming; we start from the basics. The key is consistent practice - coding is a skill you build over time.
What is the 'Bachelor's Degree Scheme in Engineering'?

That is our **Faculty-wide Common Year 1 (JS3005)**. It is perfect if you love engineering but aren't sure which specialty to pick yet. You spend the first year exploring different disciplines—Electrical, Mechanical, Aviation, etc.—and then choose your specific Major (like our Electrical or AI schemes) at the end of Year 1.
I heard PolyU is good at Electric Vehicles. Is that true?

We're really proud of our EV research! Our **Research Centre for Electric Vehicles**, led by Prof. C.C. Chan (known as the 'Father of Asian EVs'), has achieved some remarkable breakthroughs. We recently developed the world's first **Ammonia-Powered Electric Vehicle**. What's exciting for students is that you won't just read about EVs in textbooks—you could actually be testing prototypes in our Industrial Centre and working alongside researchers on cutting-edge projects.
I want to work in robotics. Is EEE the right choice?

Yes, absolutely. Robotics sits right at the intersection of electrical engineering (motors, sensors, power) and AI (control systems, computer vision). We have robotics courses and research labs where students work on autonomous systems. The AI Scheme might be particularly good if you're more interested in the intelligence side, but both schemes can lead you to robotics careers.
Tell me about the Quantum Technology research.

Quantum is the future of computing! Our **Microelectronics & Quantum Technology (MQT)** group is working on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) chips for ultra-secure communication. We're also exploring quantum algorithms for chemistry simulations. It's very advanced stuff—usually for PhDs—but as an undergraduate, you can get exposure to these concepts in your senior year electives.
How competitive is admission to EEE?

It's fairly competitive - we're one of the top engineering departments in Hong Kong. But we look at more than just HKDSE scores. We value students who show genuine interest in engineering, critical thinking, and problem-solving ability. If you've done any STEM extracurriculars, competitions, or projects, make sure to highlight those in your application.
Are there student clubs or competitions I can join?

Lots! We have the IEEE Student Branch, Robotics Club, and regular hackathons. Students also compete in international competitions like the ABU Robocon and Smart City design challenges. These are fantastic for building skills, teamwork, and your CV. Plus, they're fun and a great way to make friends who share your interests.
Is the degree accredited?

Yes, our BEng programmes are fully accredited by the **Hong Kong Institution of Engineers (HKIE)**. This is really important because it makes you eligible for **Scheme A** training, which is the fastest route to becoming a Chartered Engineer. We make sure our curriculum meets the highest professional standards.
What is 'EIE1005'?

**EIE1005 (Fundamental AI and Data Analytics)** is a core subject you take in Year 1. It introduces you to the basics of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data. It is a great way to see if you enjoy the logic and algorithms behind AI. If you like this course, you should definitely consider our **Info & AI Engineering Scheme** for your major.
Do I have to do any training in Year 1?

Yes, you will take **ENG2101 Applied Engineering Fundamentals**. This is hands-on training at our **Industrial Centre (IC)**. You will learn about 3D printing, laser cutting, and basic engineering design. It is not just theory; you actually get to build things.
What if I want to pursue a Master's or PhD later?

That's great to hear! We encourage research-minded students. You can get involved in research projects as early as Year 2 through our Undergraduate Research Scheme. Strong academic performance plus research experience can lead to postgraduate opportunities here at PolyU or at top universities worldwide. Many of our graduates go on to MIT, Stanford, Cambridge, and other leading institutions.
What is 'eMOTOR+'?

**eMOTOR+** is one of our specialized labs led by Prof. Z.Q. Zhu. It focuses on advanced motor drives. Motors are everywhere—from electric cars to industrial robots. Improving their efficiency even by 1% has a massive global energy impact. It's a very high-impact field of study.
Do you collaborate with Huawei?

Yes, we've got the **PolyU - Huawei Joint Laboratory for Optical Interconnection Network**. We collaborate on advanced optical communication systems. This is a great example of how our research is directly relevant to the biggest tech companies in the world.
我对人工智能很感兴趣，EEE适合我吗？
非常适合！我们的**资讯与人工智能工程**专业就是专门培养AI人才的。你会学到机器学习、计算机视觉、深度学习等核心技术，同时还有硬件基础，这让你比纯软件背景的同学更有竞争力。很多毕业生都进入了大厂做AI工程师。
Is the coursework more theoretical or practical?

It's a good mix. You'll definitely learn the underlying theory - Maxwell's equations, circuit analysis, signal processing - but we emphasize application. That's why we have the Industrial Centre and why WIE is mandatory. We want you to understand the 'why' behind the technology, but also be able to build and troubleshoot real systems.
What is the atmosphere like in the department?

It is collaborative and hands-on. Because we spend a lot of time in labs and the Industrial Centre, students form tight bonds. It is not just sitting in a library reading books; it is about building things together. The faculty is very approachable—we view you as junior engineers, not just students.
What is the 'Common Year 1'?

The **Common Year 1 (JS3005)** is a flexible entry route. It allows you to explore different engineering disciplines before choosing your major. However, it is **optional**. You can also apply directly to the **Electrical Scheme** or **Info & AI Scheme** if you already know what you want. Both paths share the same first-year curriculum, but direct entry secures your specific major immediately.
What are the admission requirements for JUPAS?

For **JUPAS Applicants**, we look at your HKDSE results. We typically have a high weighting for Mathematics, Physics, or ICT. However, requirements can change slightly year to year, so I always recommend checking the latest JUPAS catalogue. The key is to show a strong foundation in science and logic.
Tell me about Dr. Bonnie Law's research.

**Dr. Bonnie Law** does fascinating work in **Signal Processing** and **Forensics**. She uses technology to identify the source camera of a photo—useful for crime investigation! She also works on DNA sequence analysis. It shows how engineering skills can be applied to biology and law enforcement.
毕业论文难吗？要做什么？
毕业论文（Final Year Project, FYP）是你整个大四的核心项目。你可以选择自己感兴趣的方向——可以是研究型的、企业赞助的项目，甚至是你自己的创业想法。确实有挑战性，但也非常有意义。很多同学的FYP获奖，有的甚至申请了专利或发表了论文。
讀 Electrical Engineering 係咪好多 Math? 我驚搞唔掂。
同學，唔駛太擔心。讀 Engineering 一定要有數理基礎，Linear Algebra 同 Calculus 係基本功。不過 PolyU 有 Learning Support Centre 支援大家。其實數理只係工具，只要你對透過科技解決問題有熱誠，你一定可以掌握到。最緊要係肯試！
I am confident in my choice. How do I succeed here?

My best advice? **Be curious.** Don't just do the homework—join a competition team like Robocon, talk to your Academic Advisor, ask professors about their research. The students who get the most out of PolyU EEE are the ones who take advantage of the incredible ecosystem we've built for you. Dive in!
我英文不太好，能應付得來嗎？
這個擔憂很正常。理大所有工程課程都是全英文授課，但我們有語言支援服務，包括英文寫作中心。最重要的是不要害怕犯錯 - 大學正是提升英文的好機會。你會發現在專業環境下使用英文，進步會很快。而且同學之間平時用廣東話交流也沒問題。
I am from Mainland China. How do I apply?

For **Mainland Gaokao** students, you apply through the Non-JUPAS route based on your Gaokao scores. We value students with strong science backgrounds. You will join a vibrant community of students from all over the Mainland and Hong Kong.
返大陸實習方唔方便？
好方便！好多同學都會透過 WIE 去深圳、廣州實習，坐高鐵一個鐘就到。而且大灣區對工程師需求好大，實習機會好多。學系同內地好多科技公司都有聯繫，華為、騰訊、比亞迪呢啲大公司都會招實習生。
Do you have labs for audio processing?

Yes, we have the **PolyU – Innovation Technology (HK) Audio and Speech Signal Processing Joint Laboratory**. It is equipped with an industrial-grade acoustic room and head/torso simulators. Prof. M.W. Mak uses these facilities for his work on speech recognition and healthcare applications.
I am interested in privacy and security. Do you cover that?

Absolutely! Our **Communications & Information Security** group is really active. **Prof. Haibo Hu** is leading a project called **MyGPTShield**, which builds privacy-preserving services for LLMs. If you join the Info & AI Scheme, you'll get to work on these cutting-edge cybersecurity challenges. It's a rapidly growing field with tons of career opportunities.
What is the future of Power Engineering?

The future is **Green and Smart**! We're moving away from fossil fuels to renewables, which requires a completely new kind of 'Smart Grid' to manage the fluctuation. We're also seeing the electrification of transport. Power Engineering isn't just about cables anymore; it's about saving the planet through efficient energy systems.
听说这里的电动车研究很厉害？
是的，我们的电动车研究是世界领先的。陈清泉院士（被誉为“亚洲电动车之父”）就在我们系。我们最近还研发了氨动力电动车。如果你加入我们，不仅是学习书本知识，还有机会在实验室里接触这些最前沿的技术。
Do you offer exchange programs to other countries?

Yes, we have exchange partnerships with universities in the US, Europe, Australia, and across Asia. Many students go on semester exchanges in Year 3. It's a great way to experience different teaching styles, build an international network, and sometimes even do WIE placements abroad. The application process is competitive but definitely worth exploring.
I have family pressure to study Medicine. How do I know if engineering is right for me?

That's a tough position to be in. Here's my advice: only you can decide what's right for you. Medicine and engineering are both honorable paths, but they require different passions. Ask yourself - do you enjoy solving technical problems? Building things? Understanding how systems work? If yes, engineering might be your calling. Talk to your family about the strong career prospects and impact you can make as an engineer. Ultimately, you'll do your best work in a field you genuinely love.
Can I work on Video Coding?

Yes, **Dr. Y.L. Chan** is an expert in **Content-Aware Video Coding**. His team's using Machine Learning to improve video compression for things like 360-degree video and VR. If you're interested in how Netflix or YouTube delivers high-quality video, this is definitely the research area for you.
课程会不会很难？
难度肯定有，但我们会循序渐进。第一年打基础，数学、电路理论这些都是一步步来。到后面选专业方向，AI、电力系统、通信，你可以选自己感兴趣的深入学习。记住，工程学习本来就是要挑战自己，但只要用心学，都能掌握。
What subjects will I study in Year 1?

In the Common Year 1, you build your foundation. You will take **Calculus (AMA1110)**, **Physics**, **Computer Programming (ENG2002)**, and an introduction to **AI & Data Analytics (EIE1005)**. It is designed to give you the core skills every engineer needs, regardless of their future major.
如果我想轉科，容唔容易？
Year 1 之後轉科有一定彈性，特別係喺電機同 AI 兩個 scheme 之間。不過你要確保修咗必修課，同埋要同 academic advisor 傾。最好係一開始就諗清楚自己鍾意咩，但我哋明白同學嘅興趣會變，所以都會盡量配合。
What is the Mentorship Programme?

It's one of our best features! We pair you with experienced professionals and senior executives from the industry. Unlike a professor who teaches you theory, your mentor gives you career advice, shares industry trends, and helps you build a network. It really bridges the gap between university and the real working world.
I am interested in 5G and 6G. Do you research that?

Yes, our **Communications & Information Security** theme works heavily on this. Prof. Francis Lau is designing error-correction codes that approach the 'Shannon limit' for deep space and future networks. Prof. Liang Liu is working on **Integrated Sensing and Communication** for 6G. You will be learning from the people defining the future standards.
Is there support for academic advising?

Yes, every student is assigned an **Academic Advisor**. We have allocated time slots during the semester to meet face-to-face. Your advisor is there to help you choose subjects, plan your career, or just chat about how you are adjusting to university life. You are never alone in your journey here.
What is 'Photonic Instrumentation'?

It involves building advanced instruments using light. Our **Photonic Instrumentation Laboratory**, led by Prof. W. Jin, builds ultra-sensitive gas sensors using optical fibers. These can detect gas leaks in industry or monitor environmental pollution. It is high-precision engineering with a real social impact.
Do you have any study tours?

Yes, apart from semester-long exchanges, we organize shorter **Study Tours** during breaks. In the past, students have visited tech hubs in Mainland China, Japan, and Singapore to see engineering in action. It is a great way to see how different countries approach technology.
What is the Dragon Boat Team?

That's the fun side of EEE! We've got a departmental **Dragon Boat Team**. It's a great way to build teamwork and fitness with your classmates and even professors. Engineering can be stressful, so having a strong community and physical outlet is really important for your mental health and work-life balance.
Can I switch between Electrical and AI schemes after Year 1?

Yes, there's some flexibility, especially after Year 1 when you've had exposure to both areas. You'll need to meet with the academic advisor and ensure you've completed the prerequisite courses. That said, it's better to choose carefully from the start if possible, but we understand students' interests can evolve.
What kind of labs do we have access to?

We've got some fantastic facilities. There's the **Industrial Centre (IC)** for hands-on prototyping, power electronics labs, robotics labs, and even a clean room for semiconductor work. You'll get to use industry-standard equipment like oscilloscopes, 3D printers, and microcontroller development kits. It's not just about lectures - you'll be building real circuits and systems from Year 1.
Can I do a minor in Business while studying EEE?

Yes, you can! Many of our students combine EEE with a Business minor, especially if they're interested in tech entrepreneurship or project management. It's a smart combination - the technical depth from EEE plus business acumen makes you very marketable. Just be mindful of your workload, as EEE already has quite a few lab hours.
Can I go on exchange?

Definitely! Our **Student Exchange Programme** lets you study overseas for one semester, usually in Year 2. We've got partners like **Tampere University (Finland)** and **Jönköping University (Sweden)**. Students often tell me it's life-changing—not just academically, but because you get a completely different perspective on engineering and life. The application process is competitive though, so you'll need decent grades and a strong motivation statement.
What is 'Scheme A' training?

Scheme A is a streamlined graduate training path sanctioned by the HKIE. Because our BEng programmes are HKIE Accredited (as stated in our curriculum documents), our graduates are eligible to join Scheme A directly. This is the fastest route to becoming a Chartered Engineer, saving you years of general work experience.
毕业后能留港工作吗？
可以的！香港有IANG签证，毕业后可以留港24个月找工作。EEE毕业生在香港很受欢迎，特别是AI、数据中心、智能电网这些领域。薪资一般在2-3万港币起步，有些大公司会更高。就业率很不错，基本都能在半年内找到工作。
I am not good at exams. Is the whole degree just exams?

Not at all! While exams are necessary for checking theory, we put a huge emphasis on **Continuous Assessment** and **Practical Projects**. Your labs and your Capstone Project all count toward your grade. We want to evaluate your ability to *do* engineering, not just memorize formulas.
I am worried about finding a job after graduation.

I totally understand that anxiety—it's one of the most common concerns I hear! The good news is EEE graduates are in high demand. We have a dedicated **Placement and Job Prospects** team that organizes the Work-Integrated Education (WIE) scheme. You'll complete a minimum of 2 weeks of workplace training, though many students do much more through summer internships or industrial projects. I've seen many students secure offers from power companies, MTR, or tech giants even before they graduate. That said, the job market is competitive, so it's important to take your WIE seriously and build real skills during your studies.
If I enter via the Common Year 1, can I still study AI?

Yes, absolutely. After completing the Common Year 1 curriculum, you can choose the **Information and Artificial Intelligence Engineering Scheme** as your major. Selection is based on your Year 1 GPA, entrance score, and interview performance, so make sure you do well in your introductory subjects!
I am an international student. Will I fit in?

Absolutely! PolyU is a truly global university. We have specific admission tracks for **International Students** and a really supportive community. Since all our technical classes are taught in English, you'll have no trouble following the lectures. Plus, Hong Kong is an international hub—it's a great place to launch a global engineering career and experience Chinese culture!
Why should I choose PolyU over other universities?

PolyU EEE is unique because of our **Practical Application** focus. We don't just teach theory; we teach you how to build it. With our strong industry links, HKIE accreditation, and facilities like the Industrial Centre, we produce graduates who are ready to work on Day 1. Employers in Hong Kong know this, and that gives you an edge.
我想做 Research，係咪應該揀 EEE?
絕對係。我哋有好多世界級嘅 Research，例如陳清泉教授嘅電動車研究，仲有光纖感應器。如果你成績好，可以參加 URIS 計劃，Year 2 就可以跟教授入 Lab 做真正的科研。對於想讀 PhD 嘅同學來講係好好嘅起步。
Do international companies recruit from PolyU EEE?

Yes, definitely. We have companies like Huawei, Alibaba Cloud, Siemens, and even Google Cloud coming to our career fairs. PolyU has a strong reputation in the Greater Bay Area and increasingly internationally. Your WIE experience plus a strong final year project can make you very competitive for these roles.
Do you have Photonics research?

Yes, we are a global leader in Photonics. We have the **Photonics Research Institute** and the **Fiber Sensors and Instrumentation Laboratory**. Prof. H.Y. Tam is famous for his work on fiber optic sensors, which are used to monitor railways and bridges. If you like physics and light, this is an amazing area to specialize in.
Is there support for mental health and stress management?

Absolutely, and I'm glad you're thinking about this. PolyU has counseling services, and our department also has academic advisors who understand the pressures engineering students face. We try to create a supportive culture - it's okay to struggle, and it's okay to ask for help. Engineering is challenging, but it shouldn't come at the cost of your wellbeing.
What is 'Material Intelligence'?

Material Intelligence is a fascinating interdisciplinary field led by **Prof. H.T. Zhao**. It combines AI and robotics to synthesize new materials intelligently. Imagine a robot that 'learns' how to make better materials than a human could. It is the intersection of chemistry, robotics, and computer science.
I am an Associate Degree student. Can I apply for Senior Year?

Yes, you're exactly who we're looking for with our **Non-JUPAS Senior Year Admissions**! If you have a relevant Associate Degree or Higher Diploma, you can enter directly into Year 3. We value your prior hands-on training, so you'll skip the general first-year subjects and dive straight into the specialized major subjects. Just be aware that Year 3 is quite intensive since you're jumping right into advanced topics—but most Senior Year students adapt well because they already have practical experience.
Is there any financial help for high-achieving students?

Yes, the Department has quite a few **Scholarships** donated by industry partners and professional bodies. If you maintain strong academic performance, there's definitely recognition for that effort. It's not just about the money either—having a departmental scholarship on your resume is a great signal to future employers that you were a top performer.
How important are grades vs practical skills in getting a job?

Both matter, but in different ways. Good grades show you can learn and handle challenges. But employers also want to see hands-on skills - projects you've built, WIE experience, hackathons, or even GitHub portfolios. I'd say aim for solid grades (you don't need to be top 1%), but invest time in real-world projects. That combination is what really opens doors.
我有 Asso Degree，報唔報得 Senior Year?
可以呀，你正正係我哋 **Non-JUPAS Senior Year** 嘅對象。如果你個 Asso 係相關學科，通常可以直接入 Year 3，唔駛由頭讀起。我哋好重視你有嘅 hands-on 經驗。
I am interested in smart cities. Which major is best?

I'd recommend looking at the **Transportation Systems Engineering** major within the Electrical Scheme. Smart mobility is the backbone of a Smart City. You'd learn about signaling, traction systems, and autonomous train operations. It connects perfectly with our **PolyU-KCRC Smart Railway Research Laboratory**.
Do you have any alumni I could talk to about their experience?

That's a great idea! We have an active alumni network, and many are happy to share their experiences. You can reach out through the EEE Alumni Association, or attend our open days where we often have recent graduates talking about their career paths. LinkedIn is also useful - search for 'PolyU EEE' and you'll find lots of alumni.
What is the 'Capstone Project'?

The **Capstone Project** is your final-year masterpiece. It is a mandatory 6-credit project where you solve a complex engineering problem from scratch—design, build, and test. Many students use this to showcase their skills to future employers. It is the culmination of everything you have learned in your 4 years here.
我是内地高考生，可以报读吗？
当然可以。我们非常欢迎内地高考生通过非联招 (Non-JUPAS) 通道申请。理大 EEE 非常看重数理基础扎实的同学。在这里，你不仅能学到全英文的专业知识，还能通过‘工业中心 (IC)’获得宝贵的动手实践机会。
Can I work on Smart Grids?

Yes, Smart Grids are a major research area here. We have the **Research Centre for Grid Modernization**. We are working on using AI to manage power flow and integrate renewable energy. It is a critical field as Hong Kong and the world move towards carbon neutrality.
What is the difference between the Electrical Scheme and the AI Scheme?

That is the most common question we get! Think of it this way: The **Electrical Engineering Scheme** focuses on the physical power that drives the world—Electric Vehicles, Smart Grids, and Power Systems. The **Info & AI Engineering Scheme** focuses on the 'brains' of the system—Computer Vision, AI algorithms, and IoT. Both are crucial; one powers the city, the other makes it smart.
课程会教机器人和自动化吗？
会的！我们有专门的机器人和自动化相关课程，包括控制系统、机器视觉、传感器技术等。AI and Robotics是我们六大研究方向之一，实验室里有各种机器人平台可以让你动手实践。如果你对这方面感兴趣，还可以参加机器人竞赛，很多同学通过比赛积累了宝贵经验。
Can I take a Minor or Secondary Major if I start in Common Year 1?

Yes, definitely. Many of our students pursue a **Secondary Major** in **Innovation and Entrepreneurship (IE)** or **AI & Data Analytics (AIDA)**. It broadens your career horizons significantly. You can apply for this option starting from your second year, once you have settled into your main major.
内地学生申请难吗？需要什么条件？
通过非联招(Non-JUPAS)申请。我们主要看高考成绩，特别是数学和物理。英语也很重要，因为所有课程都是英文授课。如果你高考成绩优秀（一般要重点线以上），数理基础扎实，申请成功率还是很高的。建议尽早准备申请材料。
How do I choose my major after Common Year 1?

Towards the end of Common Year 1, there is a **Competitive Allocation** process. You rank your preferred majors (e.g., Electrical Engineering, Aviation, etc.). We look at your **Entrance Score**, your **Year 1 GPA**, and your **Interview Performance**. My advice? Show your passion during the interview—we love students who are genuinely curious about technology.
请问电机工程和AI工程有什么区别？
这其实很好区分。**电机工程 (Electrical Scheme)** 侧重于‘能源与动力’，比如电动汽车、智能电网；而 **资讯与人工智能工程 (Info & AI Scheme)** 侧重于‘算法与数据’，比如计算机视觉、物联网。两者都是核心科技，看你更喜欢硬件还是软件开发。
Can I do a minor in Japanese?

Yes, PolyU allows flexibility. You can take a **Minor** in other disciplines, including languages like Japanese, provided you manage your credits well. In fact, knowing a foreign language can be a huge asset if you want to work for international tech companies like Sony or Toyota.
How does WIE work? Do we get paid?

WIE (Work-Integrated Education) is a minimum of 2 weeks workplace training, and yes, many placements are paid - though the stipend varies by company. It's not just about the money though; it's about getting real industry exposure, understanding workplace culture, and building your professional network. Some students even turn their WIE placements into full-time job offers after graduation.
Year 1 會唔會好難頂？
Year 1 的確會有挑戰性，特別係數學同物理基礎科。但唔使太擔心，我哋會循序漸進教，由淺入深。而且有 tutorial 同 academic advisor 支援，遇到問題可以搵人幫手。最緊要係跟得上進度，唔好積落太多。好多同學一開始都會緊張，但適應咗之後就會順好多。
What's the Final Year Project (FYP) like?

The FYP is a capstone project where you work on a substantial engineering problem over your final year. You can choose a topic that interests you - could be research-based, industry-sponsored, or even your own startup idea. It's challenging but also very rewarding. Many students showcase their FYPs at exhibitions and some even win innovation awards or file patents.
I'm interested in renewable energy. Do you cover that?

Definitely. We cover solar power systems, wind energy, smart grids, and energy storage in several courses. There's also research happening in sustainable energy technologies. If this is your passion, you can choose electives focused on renewable energy and even do your FYP (Final Year Project) in this area. It's a growing field with lots of opportunities.
Are there opportunities to publish research papers as an undergraduate?

Yes, if you're involved in research through URIS (Undergraduate Research and Innovation Scheme) or working closely with a professor on their projects, you can co-author papers. It's not common for all students, but high-performing students who contribute meaningfully to research can get their names on conference or journal publications. This is a huge advantage if you're planning to pursue postgraduate studies.
What is the difference between the IoT major and the AIIE major in Info & AI Scheme?

Great question. In our **Information & AI Scheme**, the difference is about *Hardware vs. Software*. The **Electronic Systems and Internet-of-Things (ESI)** major is a BEng degree focused on the physical layer—sensors, circuits, and embedded chips. The **Artificial Intelligence and Information Engineering (AIIE)** major is a BSc degree focused on the intelligent layer—machine learning algorithms, data science, and computer vision. If you like building gadgets, choose ESI. If you like coding brains, choose AIIE.
聽講工程好多group project，我唔係好識同人合作點算？
唔使擔心，團隊合作係可以學嘅。我哋好多 project 都係小組形式，你會慢慢學識點分工、點溝通。其實工程師出到去做嘢都要同人合作，所以依家練習係好事。如果真係有困難，可以同 academic advisor 傾，我哋都會幫你融入團隊。
實驗室會唔會好危險？
唔洗擔心！我哋所有實驗室都有嚴格嘅安全措施，做實驗之前會有完整嘅安全訓練。實驗室技術員都會喺現場協助，確保所有設備正常運作。只要跟足安全指引，實驗室係好安全嘅學習環境。
What kind of AI research do you do? Is it just software?

In EEE, we do 'AI for the Physical World.' For example, **Prof. H.T. Zhao** works on **Material Intelligence**—using AI and robotics to synthesize new smart materials. We also have **Prof. Kenneth Lam** working on Computer Vision for face recognition. It is a mix of hardware and software, which is what makes our graduates so versatile.
Is it better to apply to EEE directly or via the Common Scheme?

It depends on how sure you are. If you *know* you want Electrical or AI Engineering, applying directly to our specific schemes secures your spot immediately. If you are undecided, the **Common Scheme (JS3005)** gives you time to explore. Both paths lead to the same degree in the end.
Can I take courses outside of engineering?

Yes, you'll have **General Education (GE)** requirements that let you explore humanities, social sciences, languages, and more. It's actually a great balance - you get deep technical training in EEE, but also broader perspectives through GE courses. Some students even minor in other fields like Business or Languages.
I like robots. Which scheme should I choose?

Both schemes let you work with robotics, but they approach it differently. In **Electrical Engineering**, you focus on the motors, drives, and power systems that move the robot. In **Info & AI Engineering**, you focus on the sensors, vision, and logic that guide the robot. I'd recommend checking out our **EIE Robotics Club** regardless of which one you pick—they do some really cool projects!
What's the male-to-female ratio like? Will I feel isolated as a female student?

Engineering still has more male students, but we're actively working to make it more inclusive. We have a **Women in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (WiEEE)** student chapter that organizes networking events and mentorship programs. Many of our top-performing students are women, and we're committed to creating a respectful and supportive environment for everyone.
宿舍環境點樣？
理大宿舍條件都幾好，有冷氣、WiFi、自修室。不過宿位有限，未必個個分到，所以要申請嘅話要盡早。如果冇宿舍，校外租屋都唔太遠，交通都算方便。宿舍生活對freshman嚟講係好好嘅體驗，可以識到好多唔同背景嘅朋友。
Do you do any research on renewable energy?

Yes, sustainability is a core theme for us. Our **Theme-based Smart MicroGrid Research Laboratory** works on integrating renewable energy sources like solar PV into the power grid. We also work on **Perovskite Solar Cells**, which are the next generation of flexible, high-efficiency solar technology. It's a really exciting area with huge potential.
What is 'WIE'?

**Work-Integrated Education (WIE)** is a mandatory component of your degree. It means you must complete a minimum of 2 weeks of workplace training, though options like the One-year Internship Scheme or summer internships allow for much longer experiences. We believe you can't learn engineering just by sitting in a lecture hall—you need to be out in a company, solving real problems and seeing how theory applies in practice.
Do you work on autonomous driving?

Yes, our **Electric Vehicles and Smart Mobility** group works on this. We look at 'cooperative conflict-free on-ramp merging' for connected autonomous vehicles. It uses Deep Learning to help cars talk to each other and drive safely. It is a perfect blend of AI and Transport Engineering.
I want to work in finance. Is engineering useful?

Surprisingly, yes. We have a research area in **Quantum Machine Learning** for financial modeling. Engineering teaches you rigorous data analysis and problem-solving, which FinTech companies love. Many of our graduates go into banking or quantitative analysis because they can handle the complex math.
Can I visit the labs?

We often have tours during **Info Day** or special departmental events. The **Industrial Centre** and our specialized labs like the **Smart Railway Lab** are definitely worth seeing. They are full of millions of dollars worth of equipment that you, as a student, will actually get to use.
学费和生活费大概多少？
学费方面，建议查看理大官网最新的收费标准，因为每年会有调整。生活费因人而异，住宿舍会比校外租房便宜一些，加上饮食、交通等日常开支，需要提前做好预算。好消息是我们有多种奖学金，成绩优秀的学生可以申请，能减轻不少经济负担。具体数字建议参考理大官网或联系招生办。
Do you have any support for students who want to start a company?

Absolutely! We recently established the **EEE Innovation and Engineering Hub**, which is designed specifically to support early-stage innovations (Technology Readiness Levels 1-5). We provide mentorship and can connect you with **PolyU InnoHub** for financial backing. I'll be honest though—entrepreneurship is challenging and not for everyone. But if you've got the passion and an idea worth pursuing, we want to help you become an entrepreneur, not just an employee.
Is the math very difficult in the Electrical Scheme?

I won't sugarcoat it—Electrical Engineering does rely on math to model the physical world. You'll encounter Calculus and Linear Algebra, and they can be challenging. However, we see math as a tool, not a barrier. We've got a **Learning Support Centre** specifically to help you, and most students find that if they're passionate about how things work, they'll find the motivation to master the math. It's tough, but very doable with effort.
畢業之後易唔易搵工?
絕對唔難。我哋 EEE 畢業生好搶手，兩電一鐵 (CLP, HK Electric, MTR) 每年都請好多人。再加上我哋有 WIE (工作綜合教育)，好多同學未畢業已經攞到 Return Offer。只要你肯學，搵工唔係問題。
